title: quoteShipment builds a ShippingQuote from zone rates plus one line per surcharge
subtitle: rate-calculator.ts prices transportation per parcel, then adds fuel, residential, remote-area, oversize and insurance lines
facts: resolveShippingZone maps the distance between 3-digit ZIP prefixes to zones 2-8; every cross-border shipment is zone 8
calculateBillableWeight bills the larger of actual and dimensional weight, rounded up to the half pound
Each surcharge has its own calculate* function that returns a rounded dollar amount
ShippingQuote.addLine skips zero amounts, so a quote lists only what it bills
narrative: Traced how a quote is assembled in src/shipping/rate-calculator.ts. quoteShipment validates the request, resolves the zone, bills each parcel at the larger of actual and dimensional weight and sums the transportation charge from ZONE_BASE_RATES and ADDITIONAL_POUND_RATES. Fuel, residential and remote-area surcharges are computed once from that sum; oversize and insurance are per parcel; the volume discount is added last as a negative line.

title: Remote-area surcharge applies a percentage with a minimum fee
subtitle: calculateRemoteAreaSurcharge charges a share of the transportation charge for partner-network destinations, never less than a fixed floor
facts: isRemoteAreaPostalCode decides eligibility from REMOTE_AREA_POSTAL_PREFIXES: Puerto Rico, Hawaii, Alaska, northern Canada and parts of Mexico
The percentage and the minimum fee are local constants inside calculateRemoteAreaSurcharge, not entries in the shared rate tables
The surcharge is computed from the transportation charge, before fuel and the other surcharges
narrative: Added the remote-area surcharge to quotes. quoteShipment calls calculateRemoteAreaSurcharge with the summed transportation charge and the destination address; it returns 0 unless the destination postal code starts with one of the remote-area prefixes. Finance asked to keep its two numbers next to the formula rather than in the exported tables because they are revised on a different schedule.

title: Fuel surcharge steps now counted in whole cents
subtitle: calculateFuelSurcharge skipped a step when the diesel index sat exactly on a ten-cent boundary
facts: Dividing the distance above the floor price by a fractional step is inexact in floating point, so Math.floor could land one step short
The fix rounds the distance above FUEL_INDEX_FLOOR_USD to whole cents before dividing by FUEL_INDEX_STEP_CENTS
The surcharge percentage is still capped by FUEL_SURCHARGE_CAP_PERCENT
narrative: A quote at a diesel index exactly on a ten-cent boundary came out one surcharge step low. calculateFuelSurcharge now converts the distance above the floor price to whole cents first, so every boundary lands on its own step.

title: Oversize and insurance stay per parcel; the volume discount covers transportation only
subtitle: Multi-parcel quotes list oversize handling and coverage once per parcel instead of pooling them
facts: calculateOversizeFee uses length plus girth from the sorted sides and rejects parcels above OVERSIZE_LIMITS.maximumLengthPlusGirthIn
calculateInsurance includes the first $100 of declared value and charges per started $100 above it, with a minimum charge
calculateVolumeDiscount applies the first VOLUME_DISCOUNT_TIERS entry the account reaches, to the transportation charge only
narrative: Kept oversize handling and declared-value coverage as per-parcel quote lines so a multi-parcel quote shows which parcel triggered each charge. Surcharges are never discounted: the volume discount is computed from the transportation charge alone and added as the last line.
